title: STUDY TOPIC Spiritual formation  [ the process of becoming like Jesus] part 17
scripture_text: ‘’Nevertheless, the one who receives instruction in the word should share all good things with their instructor. Do not be deceived God cannot be mocked. A man reaps what he sows. Whoever sows to please their flesh from the flesh will reap destruction; whoever sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life. Let us not become weary in doing good for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people, especially to those who belong to the family of believers.’’
devotional:
Seeds of submission. Galatians 6:8

We need to be a people that please the Spirit. When it comes to the principle of reaping and sowing we need to be people who sow to the Spirit. What does it mean to sow to the Spirit? To sow to the Spirit is to cultivate a life of dependant devotion.

Paul gives three reasons why we should sow to the spirit

If we are not sowing to the Spirit then we are sowing to the flesh/sinful nature. John Stott said this: - ‘To "sow to the flesh" is to pander to it, to cosset, cuddle and stroke it, instead of crucifying it. The seeds we sow are largely thoughts and deeds. Every time we allow our mind to harbour a grudge, nurse a grievance, entertain an impure fantasy, or wallow in self-pity, we are sowing to the flesh. Every time we linger in bad company whose insidious influence we know we cannot resist, every time we lie in bed when we ought to be up and praying, every time we read pornographic literature, every time we take a risk that strains our self-control, we are sowing, sowing, sowing to the flesh.’ “The Message of Galatians” p. 170.

Gordon Fee gives this definition for the flesh.”The flesh is the condition of humanity “before and outside of Christ.” To walk in the flesh is to walk on our own, outside of Christ’s redemptive work, outside of the power of the Holy Spirit. fairlyspiritual.org access 14/03/2025

Whether we do seemingly noble things or incredibly “wicked” things, if they are done outside of relationship with God, they are done in the flesh.

Robert Jewett defines "the flesh" in Galatians 5 and 6 as "Paul's term for everything aside from God in which one places his final trust.’ source unknown.

‘The flesh is the conviction that I am the most important thing in the universe. It is ultimately worship of myself— my pleasure, my exaltation, my success, my reputation. I will defend myself against, exalt myself over, prefer myself to any and every other person. There is an enormously self-centred core in me. Even self-destructive behaviour is an expression of personal power. If God says he loves me, I’ll destroy what he loves, to prove my superiority.’ Steve Zeisler. cdn.pbc.org

In Freudian terminology you could say that the flesh was like the ‘Id’

The id seeks instant gratification for our wants and needs. If these needs or wants aren’t met, a person can become tense, anxious, or angry. For example, Bart was stuck in traffic. He just wanted his vehicle to move! Enraged at the situation, Bart pulled his car onto the shoulder and sped forward, not caring that he was clipping people's side mirrors as he tried to get ahead of the cars in front of him.

At it’s essence our struggle with our flesh is always an identity issue. It is rooted in a wrong belief that what we have in Jesus is not enough so we develop a desire for independence from God, in order to quickly satisfy our present longings. The direction and trajectory of the flesh is always independence from God.

[b] When we are not sowing to the Spirit then we are deceiving ourselves and mocking God.

We can very easily deceive ourselves, sometimes we refuse to be honest with ourselves. We can go into performance mode in order to hide from ourselves. If everyone else thinks I am OK, then I must be!

To mock God, Greek word muckerizo, it carries the ides that we do not take what God is saying seriously. We think, it does not matter how I live, God cannot be serious, The verb he employs means literally “to turn up the nose” so as to treat with contempt. “In a culture where face and honour and shame was very important, to turn up one’s nose at someone was to shame them, it was to treat them as someone weak, as someone beneath one’s own dignity, and as unworthy of one’s respect” (Witherington, 431). The reference is not to verbal scoffing but to despising God by a whole way of life.

[c] Not to sow to the Spirit is to guarantee destruction.

The word used for destruction is phthora, this is not a sudden destruction owing to external violence, but a dissolution brought about by internal decay. It describes decomposition which brings to mind the picture of loathsome decaying matter replete with maggots and other macabre microbes! Figuratively speaking the idea is that of the horrible thought of the "rotting" of one's morals which become more depraved with greater loss of integrity as a result of "slow internal decay".

On the other hand, to sow to the Spirit is to live a life that is surrendered to the Spirit. In chapter five Paul uses four verbs to describe our relationship with the Spirit. ‘Walk by the Spirit,’ ‘Led by the Spirit.’ ‘Live by the Spirit.’ and ‘keep in step with the Spirit.’ These words carry the idea of surrender, or submitting, holding lightly to our agendas, or plans, and being open and flexible to go where the Spirit leads. It is important to recognise that when the bible talks about being led by the Spirit it is primarily talking about being led into transformation. The context of Paul’s teaching about being led by the Spirit is usually in the context of him talking about a Christian character and our transformation into the likeness of Jesus. To be led by the Spirit is to be led out of shame into grace, from guilt into freedom. from insecurity into the glorious love of God. To sow to the Spirit is to live a life that is continually in every circumstance displaying the fruit of the Spirit, no matter where we are or who we are with, or what we are doing, we recognise that the fruit of the Spirit is both appropriate and essential for that time.
prayer: Father thank you there is no situation or circumstance in life where the fruit of the Spirit is not essential.
